summary: Silent Hill entries from Sami's spine and sourced supplemental seeds, built for per-platform route research.

entries.title: Silent Hill

sami.notes: Supplemental sourced seed; not present in Sami's current spine export.

emulation.notes: Use original hardware or conservative PS1 emulation; avoid changing draw distance/fog presentation beyond tested archival preference.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PS1 presentation, optionally upscaled in emulator.

primary.why: Silent Hill is documented as a PlayStation title, with later PSN availability functioning as a digital/emulated distribution of the same original. The original PlayStation release is therefore the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version on original hardware, PS3/PSP PSN copy if already owned, or a tested PS1 emulator with original resolution/upscaling chosen before capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is known to exist; the announced remake is a separate future/modern project, not this original release route.

entries.title: Silent Hill 2

sami.notes: Supplemental sourced seed; not present in Sami's current spine export.

emulation.emulator: Native Windows PC with Enhanced Edition
emulation.notes: Use the Enhanced Edition installer/packages and test audio, FMV, and widescreen behavior before capture.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Classic PC version restored/enhanced for modern displays.

primary.why: The Xbox/Director's Cut additions, the Windows port of that expanded version, and the Enhanced Edition project improve modern compatibility, widescreen support, visuals, audio, and bugs. This gives the classic Silent Hill 2 the best complete/fidelity route without substituting the 2024 remake.
primary.how_to_play: Install the Windows Director's Cut release, apply Silent Hill 2: Enhanced Edition, enable the project's recommended widescreen/visual/audio fixes, and verify the game before a full capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not substitute the 2024 remake for this classic entry. HD Collection is listed but skipped because the sourced Enhanced Edition path is the better classic-preservation route.

sami.notes: Supplemental sourced seed; not present in Sami's current spine export.

emulation.emulator: None for primary; PCSX2 optional comparison
emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 only if the PC build loses effects/content.

primary.why: Windows is the likely highest-fidelity capture route, but it still needs a mod/compatibility pass before being treated as final.
primary.how_to_play: Capture-test the Windows version first; compare with PS2 if audio, effects, or cutscene behavior looks wrong.

sami.notes: Supplemental sourced seed; not present in Sami's current spine export.

emulation.emulator: None for primary; PCSX2/Xemu optional comparison
emulation.notes: Compare only if the PC build shows missing effects or broken behavior.

primary.why: The PC route is the highest-fidelity starting point and remains commercially accessible through GOG.
primary.how_to_play: Use the GOG build, then capture-test resolution, controller behavior, fog, audio, and cutscene playback.

entries.title: Silent Hill The Short Message

primary.why: The Short Message is a free PlayStation 5 release. No sourced PC or alternate-platform release is logged in this pass, so PS5 is the only current archive route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the native PS5 release. Capture from PS5 hardware; there is no PC/emulation primary route to prefer.

entries.remaster_caveats: If Konami later ports the game, revisit the route; current sourced data points to PS5 only.

entries.title: Silent Hill: Origins
entries.definitive_edition: Original PSP version, with PS2 as comparison/access route

emulation.emulator: PPSSPP for PSP primary if hardware capture is unavailable
emulation.notes: Use accurate settings and document upscaling or texture options.

primary.why: Origins was designed and released first for PSP, with the later PS2 version acting as a port. For the main route, preserve the PSP original through hardware or accurate PPSSPP capture; use PS2 only as a comparison or accessibility route.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned PSP copy on hardware or PPSSPP with accurate settings. Record region, revision, display scaling, controls, audio settings, and whether the PS2 port was compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Compare only if documenting platform differences or if PSP capture is unavailable.
secondary.why: The PS2 port is useful but not the original design target.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced modern official remaster replaces the PSP/PS2 routes.

entries.title: Silent Hill: Downpour
entries.definitive_edition: Patched Xbox 360 version via Xbox backward compatibility, with PS3 comparison if needed

emulation.emulator: RPCS3 / Xenia only for preservation testing
emulation.notes: Original hardware or Xbox backward compatibility is preferred; document emulator compatibility if used.

primary.version: Patched Xbox 360 version via original hardware or Xbox One/Series backward compatibility
primary.why: Downpour was released only on PS3 and Xbox 360. The Xbox route has backward-compatibility access on modern Xbox consoles, while PS3 is the other original hardware route; both should log patch/performance state because technical issues were part of the release context.
primary.how_to_play: Use an Xbox 360 disc/digital copy on Xbox 360 or supported Xbox backward compatibility where available. Record platform, patch, disc/digital state, difficulty, ending route, side quests, 3D use, and whether PS3 was compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Use if documenting PS3-specific performance and patch state.
secondary.why: The game launched on both HD consoles and performance/patch differences matter.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record platform, patch, performance, disc/digital state, endings, and side quests.

entries.title: Silent Hill: Homecoming
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC release with compatibility fixes documented

emulation.notes: Use native PC route; RPCS3/Xenia only for console comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Patched PC release or original PS3/Xbox 360 hardware

primary.version: Current Steam PC release with fixes documented
primary.why: Homecoming has an available PC route, unlike several other Silent Hill entries, but the PC version needs compatibility and control/fix notes. The PS3/Xbox 360 versions are valid original-console routes and should be compared if console performance or patch behavior matters.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam PC release with community fixes as needed. Record storefront/build, OS, compatibility fixes, controller, resolution, difficulty, ending route, and whether PS3/Xbox 360 was compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Use if documenting console performance or control behavior.
secondary.why: The PC route is easiest for capture, but the console versions are the original release context.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record fixes, input, platform, patch state, and ending route.

entries.title: Silent Hill: Shattered Memories
entries.definitive_edition: Wii original with real Wii Remote controls

emulation.emulator: Dolphin only with verified Wii Remote behavior
emulation.notes: Original Wii hardware is preferred; document emulator/controller if used.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Wii hardware with Wii Remote

primary.why: Shattered Memories was designed around Wii pointer/phone/flashlight interaction and later ported to PS2 and PSP. The Wii version is the main fidelity route, while PS2/PSP are access/performance variants.
primary.how_to_play: Use a Wii copy on Wii or Wii U backward compatibility with a real Wii Remote and nunchuk. Record region, controller setup, profile choices, ending, optional photos/messages, and whether PS2/PSP versions were compared.

secondary.what_to_play: Use if documenting non-Wii control behavior.
secondary.why: They are ports of a Wii-designed experience.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record profile choices, ending, controller setup, and platform branch.
